generatedBy: /audit skill v1.0 — S201 merge (S200 baseline + S201 conversion/AI/loop items)

topline.thesis: S201 audit fuses S200 visual-elevation items with a new conversion + intelligence + feedback layer. Signal fix session revealed 9 high-priority items the S200 audit missed: the /membership/ page has no AI advisor or progressive disclosure (the single highest-ROI conversion fix on the site); FAQ is still static HTML; no referrer-source enters the funnel; IGNIS synthesis has no save/share; rank progress has no shareable card; theme doesn't follow members cross-device; lore is ungated; derive scripts aren't in npm run build. These 9 items (combined priority 509) dwarf the remaining S200 visual carries (233.5), making the S201 plan primarily conversion + intelligence depth and secondarily visual finish.

items.title: IGNIS tier advisor on /membership/ — 'Not sure? Ask IGNIS'
items.why: The /membership/ conversion page has no intelligent decision aid — visitors who don't know which tier fits them bounce rather than ask. A 'Which tier is right for me?' input box beneath the tier grid routes to /ignis/ with a pre-seeded context string, turning IGNIS into the studio's conversion assistant. This is a one-hour ship with session-long payoff.
items.recipe: Add an `.ignis-tier-advisor` section below `.mem-tiers-grid` in membership/index.html: form with input + 'Ask IGNIS →' button. On submit, redirect to `/ignis/?q=Which+tier+fits+me%3F+` + encodeURIComponent(userInput). Wire `funnel:membership_ignis_query` to /v/rum + add to RUM_UX_EVENTS in src/worker.js. No backend changes.

L3.recipe: Embedded IGNIS widget (fetch-based) that answers inline without leaving the page. Supabase session injected so signed-in members get personalized advice.

items.title: Persist theme choice to Supabase profile — syncs across devices for signed-in members
items.why: Theme selection lives in localStorage only — a member who chooses 'Lava' on desktop gets the default theme on mobile. For a membership product where identity is central, having your aesthetic follow you is a small but memorable detail. Supabase already tracks member preferences; adding a `theme` column is a trivial migration.

In `assets/theme.js`, after a theme change, call `supabase.from('profiles').update({theme}).eq('id', user.id)` if session exists. On page load (after auth check in identity.js bootstrap), read `profile.theme` and apply before CSS paints to avoid FOUC. ~2h.
